parsed.why: Ranked among worst states for anti-trans laws; state-run facility restrictions reach visitors, closed birth-certificate rules, no state discrimination or hate-crime cover, hostile party framing; only tribal third-gender traditions cut the other way.

Low-risk tier with operating anti-discrimination enforcement, no surgery barrier, X markers, city sanctuary shielding travellers; parental passport/entry regime still binds, and no statewide hate-crime or public-accommodation statute limits the upside.

Low-risk ranked and locally non-hostile, but a national legislature imposed the facilities restriction and arrested protesters there; national custody and document regime apply directly with no local buffer, and durability is explicitly doubted.

Facility ban is school-only, limiting visitor exposure, but statewide public-accommodations gap plus religious-refusal statute gives thin recourse against service denial; hate-crime law excludes gender identity and vetoes were overridden on care and sport.

Public-accommodation and hate-crime coverage with reporting machinery, self-declared documents, X markers and a care shield law protecting visitors; unenforced sodomy statutes are latent only; shared national entry and custody regime caps the score.
